# `Q-3-50` — LineBlock Not Supported in ANSI Format

> LineBlock elements cannot be rendered in ANSI terminal output.

## What this means

A line block is a block of text written with leading `|`
characters, where each line is preserved as a separate line in
the output — useful for verse, addresses, or other line-broken
prose. The ANSI writer (used when rendering to a terminal) does
not yet support this construct, and emits the error rather than
silently flattening the lines into a paragraph.

## Why this happens

Your document contains a line block (lines beginning with `| `)
and you rendered to ANSI output.

## How to fix

Two options:

- **Render to a different format.** HTML, PDF, and the other
  markdown writers handle line blocks correctly.
- **Rewrite the line block** as a paragraph with hard line
  breaks (two trailing spaces, or a backslash at end of line)
  if the visual result is acceptable for your use case.

## Related

- `Q-3-51`, `Q-3-52`, `Q-3-53`, `Q-3-54`, `Q-3-55` — other
  block types the ANSI writer does not yet support.
